boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named River Campus spaces with documented ways students can study, gather, play, reflect, or organize.

cards.title: Wilson Commons
cards.subtitle: River Campus center for student life
cards.notes: Use the public lounges for a casual meet-up or reset between classes; check the building hours before planning a longer stay.
cards.short_summary: A five-floor campus center with space for meetings, events, relaxation, recreation, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Wilson Commons as a central campus-life location with space for meetings, special events, relaxation, recreation, and dining.
cards.source_title: Wilson Commons, designed by I.M. Pei: A centerpiece of campus life
cards.access_notes: Public lounges are available for general student use when the building is open; other spaces may require reservations.

cards.title: Frederick Douglass Commons
cards.subtitle: Campus Center student-life space
cards.notes: Meet collaborators in a public lounge during open building hours, then use the nearby plaza only if it is not reserved for an event.
cards.short_summary: One of the Campus Center locations whose public lounges are designated for general student use.
cards.evidence_claim: University Student Activities lists Douglass Commons as a Campus Center student-life space and says its public lounges are available for general student use when open.
cards.access_notes: Public lounges are not reservable and are available for general student use when the building is open.

cards.title: Dandelion Square
cards.subtitle: Outdoor space by Wilson Commons and Goergen Athletic Center
cards.notes: Pause by the clock tower before an activity or use the square as a waypoint; event use is coordinated with other outdoor-space reservations.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor square at the front of Wilson Commons and the Goergen Athletic Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The University places Dandelion Square in front of Wilson Commons and the Goergen Athletic Center and identifies it as reservable with outdoor spaces.
cards.access_notes: May be reserved in conjunction with other outdoor spaces; do not assume an event setup is open for drop-in use.

cards.entity_name: Janis and James S. Gleason Library
cards.title: Gleason Library
cards.subtitle: Rush Rhees Library, first floor
cards.notes: Choose a quiet seat for solo work or book a group studio when available; the space supports both individual and collaborative study.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour-during-semester library space with quiet areas, varied seating, and group studios.
cards.evidence_claim: Gleason Library offers individual and collaborative study options, quiet space, and six group studios; it remains open 24 hours during the semester.
cards.access_notes: The library states that the space remains open 24 hours during the semester; consult the current library-hours listing for exceptions.

cards.title: Great Hall
cards.subtitle: Rush Rhees Library, second floor
cards.notes: Settle in for quiet reading or meet a classmate before heading to nearby Humanities Center and Digital Scholarship Lab entrances.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study and exhibition space that also functions as a hub inside Rush Rhees Library.
cards.evidence_claim: River Campus Libraries describes the Great Hall as a quiet study and exhibition space, with entrances to several library and academic units.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Rush Rhees Library; follow current library access and hours guidance.

cards.title: Study Zone
cards.subtitle: Learning Center, Dewey Hall 1-160 suite
cards.notes: Apply or enroll before relying on this low-distraction room, then check in with a Study Zone Leader and plan a focused work block.
cards.short_summary: A staffed, low-distraction study setting that pairs accountability with peer support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Center calls Study Zone a quiet, low-distraction place to work where students commit to at least three hours weekly and receive peer support.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires enrollment; it operates in fall and spring, closes during summer and winter breaks, and participants check in on arrival.

cards.title: Spurrier Gymnasium
cards.subtitle: Spurrier Hall recreation space
cards.notes: Bring non-marking sneakers and swipe in with your UR ID when the court is unreserved; ask the manager desk about signing out equipment.
cards.short_summary: A hardwood gym with basketball, volleyball, badminton, and wrestling facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that UR community members may use Spurrier Gymnasium with a UR ID when the space is not reserved, and may sign out sports equipment.
cards.access_notes: UR community members use UR ID swipe access when no reservation is in place; guests must remain with a University community member.

cards.title: Goergen Athletic Center
cards.subtitle: River Campus Sports Complex
cards.notes: Check recreation access and available courts before going, then choose an open-recreation or club-sport facility that fits your group’s plans.
cards.short_summary: A major athletic complex with fitness, field house, gymnasium, aquatic, squash, and recreation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies Goergen Athletic Center as the centerpiece of the River Campus Sports Complex and lists facilities supporting open recreation, intramurals, and club sports.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Athletics and Recreation facility access rules, programming, and reservations.

cards.title: Interfaith Chapel
cards.subtitle: 1045 Wilson Boulevard, River Campus
cards.notes: Visit for quiet reflection, a faith-community gathering, or dialogue; check the chapel calendar and room availability before arranging a group visit.
cards.short_summary: A multi-faith gathering place with worship, dialogue, meditation, and community space.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes the Interfaith Chapel as a place where people of different faiths or none can share dialogue, worship, and interfaith education.
cards.access_notes: The chapel welcomes varied faith traditions and reservations depend on availability; confirm a specific gathering or room before visiting.

cards.title: Genesee Hall
cards.subtitle: First-Year Hill shared-use building
cards.notes: For an organized study group or workshop, identify an available meeting room through campus processes; residential lounges remain for residents’ use.
cards.short_summary: A first-year residence building with meeting rooms for study groups and workshops plus student-life and athletics spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: University Event and Classroom Management says Genesee Hall includes meeting rooms for study groups and workshops, alongside residential and athletics facilities.
cards.source_title: Genesee Hall | Event and Classroom Management
cards.access_notes: The building includes residential floors; access to residential lounges and other rooms may be limited to residents or scheduled users.
